title: Canary Islands record about 1,500 boat arrivals in one day as El Hierro's emergency grows
seoTitle: Canary Islands migrants: record day, El Hierro emergency
dek: On 14 November the islands recorded their highest daily number of boat arrivals: 1,488 people by Euronews' count, more than 1,500 by RTVE's, most of them on El Hierro, an island of about 12,000 people that has received more than 9,000 since the start of November.
happened: On 6 November the Cabildo, El Hierro's island council, declared a social emergency by decree of its president, Alpidio Armas, and asked higher authorities for help. It says more than 8,000 people arrived in the past five weeks, and more than 3,000 in five days aboard about 30 boats. Overnight from 5 to 6 November rescuers brought at least 1,021 people ashore on El Hierro, Gran Canaria and Lanzarote, one of whom had died, according to EFE and the maritime rescue service. EFE counted 307 minors and 11 babies among about 2,300 people who reached El Hierro in the first five days of November; most boats left from Senegal. Interior Ministry figures show 6,194 sea arrivals to the Canary Islands in October, nearly five times as many as in October 2025, while the total from January to October, 13,327, was slightly below the same period of 2025 and well below 2024's 34,087. On Saturday, 14 November, 1,488 people arrived across the Canary Islands, Euronews reports, beating the previous daily record of 1,461 set on 7 November 2020; RTVE, cited by DPA, counted more than 1,500. Twelve to thirteen large boats reached El Hierro, carrying 1,235 people, with one more boat each reaching Gran Canaria and Tenerife. At least 120 of the arrivals were minors. DPA reports El Hierro has received more than 9,000 people on 91 boats since the start of November. Most come from Senegal, Gambia, Mauritania and Guinea; a crossing can take up to a week.

sides.says: Armas said the situation "has been getting worse in recent days" and that "El Hierro cannot face this alone" (translated from Spanish). The council asks for more staff, with rotation so workers can rest, for the maritime rescue service, health service, security forces, Red Cross and NGOs; coordinated transfers of people to islands with more capacity; and reinforced first-reception facilities. It has opened temporary reception centres to ease pressure on the main centre in San Andrés, and wants measures for residents, fishers and businesses in the port of La Restinga.

President Fernando Clavijo called the situation "absolutely unsustainable", warned that it "is going to get worse", and asked for an urgent meeting with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. He wants more resources from the central government, closer coordination and more involvement from the European Union, especially for El Hierro's strained health services. On 14-15 November he wrote to EU Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner asking for urgent action on the Atlantic route and demanded that aid agreed with Madrid be delivered immediately: more accommodation, better medical care and faster transfers to other islands and mainland Spain. Canary authorities attribute the surge partly to Senegal's security forces being redeployed to sporting events in Dakar.

Dozens of people protested at the port where boats are brought ashore. One said: "We are here because everyone looks the other way." Local fishers said they could not get in or out of the port to work. Txema Santana, a former migration adviser to the Canary government, says residents are protesting the authorities' slow response, not the migrants.

DPA reports the government has declared a migration emergency for El Hierro. According to Clavijo, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez pledged to urgently convene the interministerial commission on immigration, and Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres was due to visit La Restinga on 15 November.

next: Rescue operations continued on 15 November, when at least four more boats reached El Hierro. Clavijo wants the measures agreed with Madrid carried out immediately, and El Hierro's council warns pressure could keep rising in the coming weeks.
summary: The Canary Islands recorded their highest daily number of boat arrivals on 14 November, about 1,500 people, most of them landing on El Hierro, an island of about 12,000 people that has received more than 9,000 since the start of November and declared a social emergency on 6 November. Most people come from Senegal, Gambia, Mauritania and Guinea, and at least 120 of that day's arrivals were minors. The Canary government is pressing Madrid and the EU for staff, accommodation and faster transfers; Madrid has declared a migration emergency for the island.

conflicts: Arrivals in early November: El Hierro's council says more than 3,000 in five days; EFE's tally cited by Anadolu gives about 2,300 for the island in the first five days of November (and more than 3,200 for all the Canary Islands).

Minors on 14 November: Euronews gives 167 (provisional); DPA, citing RTVE, says at least 120.
